# Language

The lexical and resolution surface of the Ono language: keywords, operators, argument modes, literals, types, names and statements. Rendered from `docs/contracts/language.yaml`, which restates what `docs/contracts/grammar.ebnf` implies and is what help and completion read (spec §46.3); where the two could disagree, the grammar wins.

## Keywords

A word is a keyword only where the grammar asks for one; in a words-mode argument `let` is the word "let" (ADR-0009).

| kind | keywords |
|---|---|
| statement | `let`, `fn`, `alias`, `if`, `else`, `for`, `while`, `match`, `try`, `catch`, `return`, `break`, `continue`, `use` |
| expression | `and`, `or`, `not`, `in` |
| literal | `true`, `false`, `null` |
| reserved | `elif`, `until` — Reserved, not implemented. ADR-0009 and grammar.ebnf list them among the expression-mode heads; the grammar spells the constructs `else if` and `while`. They are reserved so that a future spelling cannot silently change the meaning of an existing script. |

## Operators

### In expressions

Lowest precedence first; a higher rank binds tighter.

| operator | precedence | associativity | arity | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `or` | 1 | left | binary | Logical disjunction over truth values. |
| `and` | 2 | left | binary | Logical conjunction over truth values. |
| `==` | 3 | left | binary | Equality. Compares values, converting compatible units first. |
| `!=` | 3 | left | binary | Inequality. |
| `<` | 4 | left | binary | Less than. A comparison only in expression mode; a redirection in words mode. |
| `<=` | 4 | left | binary | Less than or equal. |
| `>` | 4 | left | binary | Greater than. A comparison only in expression mode; a redirection in words mode. |
| `>=` | 4 | left | binary | Greater than or equal. |
| `in` | 5 | left | binary | List or range membership. |
| `not in` | 5 | left | binary | Negated membership. |
| `~=` | 5 | left | binary | Regex match. Spec §6.3 requires regex to be an explicit operator, never implicit. |
| `!~=` | 5 | left | binary | Negated regex match. |
| `+` | 6 | left | binary | Addition; also duration and byte-size arithmetic within one dimension. |
| `-` | 6 | left | binary | Subtraction; also timestamp minus duration. |
| `*` | 7 | left | binary | Multiplication. |
| `/` | 7 | left | binary | Division. In words mode a bare `/` is part of a path word, never division. |
| `%` | 7 | left | binary | Remainder. Adjacent to a numeric literal it is instead the percent unit suffix. |
| `not` | 8 | prefix | unary | Logical negation. |
| `-` | 8 | prefix | unary | Arithmetic negation. |
| `.` | 9 | left | postfix | Field access. `process.user.name`. |
| `?.` | 9 | left | postfix | Null-safe field access: yields null instead of an error when the receiver is null. |
| `[]` | 9 | left | postfix | Index or key lookup. |
| `()` | 9 | left | postfix | Function call. |

### Between pipelines and stages

| operator | meaning |
|---|---|
| `\|` | Connect one stage's output to the next stage's input. |
| `&&` | Run the next pipeline only if this one succeeded. Chains on exit status, not on truth. |
| `\|\|` | Run the next pipeline only if this one failed. |
| `&` | Detach the pipeline into a job (spec §18.4). Every backgrounded line runs on an evaluator of its own, on a copy of the session's scopes, that never reads the terminal (ADR-0952, ADR-0958); it keeps the directory it was started in and refuses `cd` (ADR-0955, ADR-0957), and its result is bounded by `limits.command_capture_bytes`. `fg` waits for it and shows its result once, `kill %N` stops it with its children, and every job ends with the shell (ADR-0959). |
| `;` | End a statement. |

### Redirection

Redirections exist only on words-mode stages, which are exactly the stages that produce bytes (ADR-0009). A structured pipeline must pass through a serializer before it may reach a byte sink, which spec §12.5 requires in any case.

| form | meaning |
|---|---|
| `>` | Redirect stdout to a file, truncating it. |
| `>>` | Redirect stdout to a file, appending. |
| `<` | Redirect stdin from a file. |
| `>&` | Duplicate an output file descriptor onto another, as in `2>&1`. |
| `<&` | Duplicate an input file descriptor onto another. |

A decimal file descriptor may prefix any redirection with no intervening space, as in `2>`.

## Argument modes

The mode is a property of the head word, known before any registry is loaded, so the editor parses a line as it is typed (ADR-0009).

**`words`** (the default) — Every head not listed as expression-mode: external commands, native verb-target commands, and `to` / `from` / `format`. `<` `>` `>>` are redirections; bare words are word atoms and keep their exact source text, so an external command receives what was typed.

**`expression`** — `<` and `>` are comparisons; a bare identifier that is not a keyword and is not followed by `(` is a field path, so `select pid name cpu` and `sort cpu desc` need no quoting. No redirection is possible.

Heads: `where`, `select`, `sort`, `group`, `take`, `skip`, `each`, `reduce`, `count`, `measure`, `join`, `diff`, `if`, `elif`, `while`, `until`, `let`, `return`, `match`.

Options read in this mode on a head of the other one:

| head | option | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `find` | `--where` | The predicate of `find place` (v0.4 §6.8): read in expression mode, so `>` compares and a bare identifier is a field path of the object being searched for. |

## Escapes between the modes

- **Words into an expression**, `( … )`: A parenthesised value inside a words-mode argument, e.g. `echo (get process | count)`.
- **An expression into words**: A quoted string is a word wherever a word is expected; a word is never re-lexed as an operator.

## Unit suffixes

A numeric literal immediately followed by a suffix is a semantic scalar: `512MiB` is one token, `512 MiB` two (spec §10.6). Comparisons convert compatible units and refuse incompatible dimensions with `type.invalid_unit` (Ono-Sendai-E0203).

### `bytesize`

Data sizes. Both the binary (IEC) and the decimal (SI) families are accepted and are not the same.

| suffix | factor | unit |
|---|---|---|
| `B` | 1 | byte |
| `KiB` | 1024 | kibibyte |
| `MiB` | 1048576 | mebibyte |
| `GiB` | 1073741824 | gibibyte |
| `TiB` | 1099511627776 | tebibyte |
| `PiB` | 1125899906842624 | pebibyte |
| `KB` | 1000 | kilobyte |
| `MB` | 1000000 | megabyte |
| `GB` | 1000000000 | gigabyte |
| `TB` | 1000000000000 | terabyte |
| `PB` | 1000000000000000 | petabyte |

### `duration`

Spans of time. `m` is minutes; there is no month suffix, because a month is not a fixed span.

| suffix | factor | unit |
|---|---|---|
| `ns` | 1 | nanosecond |
| `us` | 1000 | microsecond |
| `ms` | 1000000 | millisecond |
| `s` | 1000000000 | second |
| `m` | 60000000000 | minute |
| `h` | 3600000000000 | hour |
| `d` | 86400000000000 | day |
| `w` | 604800000000000 | week |

### `ratio`

A proportion. `24.8%` is the float 0.248 carrying a percent unit; spec §33.5 requires serialization to emit the canonical value, not the display string.

| suffix | factor | unit |
|---|---|---|
| `%` | 0.01 | percent |

## Literals

| literal | forms | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| integer | `42`, `-7`, `0x1f`, `0b1010`, `1_000_000` | Decimal, hexadecimal and binary; `_` is a digit separator. There is no octal literal. |
| float | `1.5`, `2.5e-3` | Decimal fraction with an optional exponent. |
| string, double-quoted | escapes `\\`, `\"`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`, `\e`, `\xNN`, `\u{…}`; interpolation `$name`, `$name.field`, `$( … )` | Escapes and interpolation both apply. |
| string, single-quoted | — | Raw: no escapes and no interpolation. A literal single quote can only be written in the double-quoted form. |
| string, unterminated | — | An unterminated string is `parse.incomplete` (Ono-Sendai-E0002), never `parse.syntax`, so the editor can tell "still typing" from "wrong". |
| regex | `/…/flags`; flags `i`, `m`, `s`, `x` | A regex literal only in expression mode at operand position. In words mode `/etc/passwd` is a path word. |
| timestamp | `2000-01-01T00:00:00Z` | An instant, in the RFC 3339 profile of ISO 8601 (spec §6.3 dates, §10.2): a full date, `T`, a time and a zone. Only in expression operand position; a date alone is not a literal (ADR-0071). |
| boolean | `true`, `false` | — |
| null | `null` | Unknown or unavailable data. Never fabricated and never zero (spec §10.5). |

## Types

The value types of spec §10.2, as schemas and `let`/`fn` annotations name them (ADR-0012).

Scalars: `null`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, `decimal`, `string`, `bytes`, `path`, `timestamp`, `duration`, `bytesize`, `regex`, `uuid`, `ip`, `ipnetwork`, `port`.

| type | meaning |
|---|---|
| `list<T>` | An ordered sequence. |
| `map<K,V>` | An association from keys to values. |
| `record` | A map-like value with a stable schema and an optional semantic type name. |
| `stream<T>` | A lazily produced sequence, possibly unbounded. |
| `enum` | A closed set of named values, enumerated by the schema field that uses it. |
| `error` | A structured error; `ono.error/1`. Spec §25 makes it a variant of Value. |
| `ref<schema-id>` | An identity handle for an object of that schema: its identity fields plus a display name, resolvable to the full record. A ref that cannot be resolved keeps the numeric identity it was built from (spec §23.6). |
| `<schema-id>` | A bare schema id as a type means an embedded record of that schema, in contrast to `ref<…>` (ADR-0012). |
| `value` | Any value of the model. Used where a field genuinely spans the union, such as `ActionResult.target` (ADR-0012). |

## Names

**Variables** are `$name`, with field access `$name.field.field`. `$env`: The environment record; `$env.PATH` is the environment variable. A bare `$NAME` resolves the shell binding if one exists and otherwise the environment variable of that name; the order is fixed and inspectable through `explain` (ADR-0009).

| token | meaning |
|---|---|
| `@` | The item bound by the enclosing block (spec §19.4), or the interactive selection at the prompt (spec §6.4). |
| `@-N` | The Nth previous pipeline result. `@-1` is the previous one. |
| `@N` | Item N of the current result. |

**Namespaces**, `<namespace>:<name>`: A qualified head forces one stage of the resolution order and skips the rest. A qualified name that does not resolve is `resolve.command_not_found` and is never silently retried in another namespace (ADR-0011). A head containing `/` is never a namespace: `./build.sh` and `/usr/bin/env` are paths.

| prefix | resolves in | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ono:` | native command registry | Native commands only, including KUANG/11 contributions. |
| `exec:` | PATH | External executables only. |
| `fn:` | user functions | User functions only. |
| `<module>:` | module or KUANG/11 package | Commands contributed by that module or package (spec §19.6, §31.22). Publisher-namespaced ids (spec §31.5) mean a package can always be addressed unambiguously. |

## Resolution order

A head word resolves in exactly this order, first match wins (ADR-0011, resolving the "suggested default" of spec §6.5). `explain <command>` reports which step matched, what was skipped and why — the order is reported by the code, not merely documented beside it.

| step | kind | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | keyword | A language keyword or control form. |
| 2 | function | A user function, in the innermost scope that defines one — in every stage of a pipeline, not only the first. A call after another stage reads that stage's stream through its body (ADR-0951). |
| 3 | alias | An alias. Expanded exactly once, then re-resolved from step 1, so an alias may shadow a native command and a cycle terminates. |
| 4 | native | The native command registry, including KUANG/11 contributions. |
| 5 | external | The first executable hit on PATH, with the usual executable-bit rules. |
| 6 | failure | resolve.command_not_found (Ono-Sendai-E0101), with edit-distance suggestions over natives, functions, aliases and PATH (spec §15.4). |

Two contributed commands claiming one unqualified name is `resolve.ambiguous` (Ono-Sendai-E0103), listing every candidate's qualified name. Steps 1–5 are ordered, and the core never allows two natives to claim one name (spec §40.1).

## Statements

| form | meaning |
|---|---|
| `let name [: type] = pipeline` | Declare or rebind a binding in the current scope (spec §19.2). The only binding form; rebinding is a further `let`. |
| `fn name(param: Type = default, …) -> Type { … }` | Declare a function (spec §19.3). A call stands in any stage of a pipeline. At the head, its body produces the stream the stages after it read; a body that is one pipeline streams into them, any other is collected first (v0.4.1 §26.2, ADR-0481, ADR-0950). After another stage, its body must be one pipeline whose first stage reads a stream — a transform, `each { … }`, or a call of the same shape — and that stage reads the stream in front of the call; any other body is refused with `type.mismatch` before anything runs (ADR-0951). |
| `alias name = pipeline` | Declare an alias (spec §6.5 step 2). Its text replaces the head word that names it, exactly once, and the result is resolved again from step 1 (ADR-0070). |
| `if expr { … } else if expr { … } else { … }` | Conditional (spec §19.5). |
| `for name in expr { … }` | Iterate over a list or stream. |
| `while expr { … }` | Loop while the expression holds. |
| `match expr { pattern => { … }, … }` | Pattern match. |
| `try { … } catch name { … }` | Catch a structured error as a value; match on its `name` selector (ADR-0006). |
| `return expr?` | Return from a function. |
| `break` | Leave the innermost loop. |
| `continue` | Continue the innermost loop. |
| `use module` | Bring a module's contributions into scope (spec §19.6). |

## Blocks and records

`{ … }` is a record when the first significant token after `{` is an identifier or string followed by `:`, and `{}` is the empty record; otherwise it is a block. One token of lookahead, which the incremental parser can always perform (ADR-0009).

```text
{name: "x", port: 80}
each { restart service @ }
```

## Comments

`#` — From `#` to end of line, when `#` begins a token.

## Built-in functions

| function | returns | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `now()` | `timestamp` | The current wall-clock time. Spec §6.3 uses it in `modified < now() - 7d`. v0.5 §28.3 keeps it meaning real current time even under a historical coordinate; the instant a query evaluates at is `context.time`. |
| `age(timestamp)` | `duration` | How long ago an instant was — `now() - t` (v0.5 §28.3). An argument that is not an instant is unknown, never a fabricated span (ADR-0014). |
| `between(timestamp, from, to)` | `bool` | Whether an instant falls inside a window, both ends included (v0.5 §28.3). An undecided argument makes the answer unknown. |
